I remember my grandfather pulling his truck up the driveway backwards with the bed holding a new RCA console color TV back in 1970. I ran outside to see what the was going on as he and a neighbor unloaded it from the truck and carried it into the living room. I was so excited that there was this huge 25" screen staring me in the face. It was the most amazing thing ever since up till that point we were watching a 13" B/W TV that sat on top of a TV dinner stand. After what seemed like an eternity of antenna wiring and futzing about to get a signal in clear I was finally able to see a glorious full color TV world unfurl before my eyes. It was amazing but what really changed my TV watching existence was when The Wizard of Oz showed on that console TV for the first time and my whole family awed at the fantastic colors after Dorothy opened the door of the farmhouse relocated by the tornado.Jaws dropped and cheers were a-plenty. My grandfather kept that console TV the rest of his life although in its later years it only served as a stand for a new TV, VCR and later a DVD player. So many fond memories of that TV still fill my head. No other TV has impacted my life quite the same way as that one. It's sad to see how little excitement modern TVs bring out in us today. I sure do miss that old console TV and my grandfather who watched it like clockwork till the 10 o'clock news was over.
